commits.edited_message:
knownhost: match equivalent IPv6 literals

Plain known-host entries are currently compared as text, so equivalent
expanded and compressed IPv6 literals do not match.

This change keeps the existing exact-string fast path and compares two
valid plain IPv6 literals by their 128-bit address. It also supports
bracketed IPv6 host-and-port entries while requiring the port suffix to
match exactly.

No DNS lookup is performed. Hostname matching and the CUSTOM and hashed
known-host paths remain unchanged.

Plain host tokens and hashed-host salts are measured against the scratch
buffer size, so a token that fills every byte except the terminating NUL
is accepted.

Reported-by: Krisscut on github
Fixes #1398

Closes #2568

scp: handle `ssh2_snprintf()` failure in `scp_send()`

It could happen with base paths too large to fit into the 256-byte
response buffer.

Reported-by: QcN3ep

name the hashed-host token limit the same way as the plain and salt limits.

coupling: The NUL stored after a known-host token is one past the end of a scratch array only when that array and its length check disagree, and each disagreement is split across two of the three commits. 680db00 names KNOWNHOST_PLAIN_MAX (256) and KNOWNHOST_SALT_MAX (32) and points the plain-host and salt checks at those macros instead of sizeof(buf)-1, while the arrays stay 256 and 32, so a token that fills every byte but the NUL still fits. 328e421 sizes the plain-host scratch buffer to HOST_NAME_MAX (255) and names KNOWNHOST_HASH_MAX (256), retargeting the hashed-host check; the hashed hostbuf is still 256 in that commit, and without 680db00 the plain-host check remains sizeof-based, so both stores stay in range. b85bbe1 drops the spare byte on the hashed-host buffers (saltbuf 32 to 31, hostbuf 256 to 255); its checks still follow sizeof(buf)-1 unless an earlier commit retargeted them. Plain hostbuf[namelen] at namelen 255 needs 680db00's check and 328e421's 255-byte array. Hashed hostbuf[hostlen] at hostlen 255 needs 328e421's KNOWNHOST_HASH_MAX and b85bbe1's 255-byte array. saltbuf[saltlen] at saltlen 31 needs 680db00's KNOWNHOST_SALT_MAX and b85bbe1's 31-byte array. Reverting any one commit restores either the sizeof check or the larger array at every site that commit touches, and the other pair still overflows. The probe feeds all three lines, so a single-commit repair leaves a later (or the first) line reaching the remaining store. A repair has to put each named limit back in agreement with the array written by a different commit.
